h: From the park to the River Dart
p: Woodlands works best as a whole-day outing. With water rides, indoor play, animals and falconry all on site, there's enough to keep a family busy from morning until late afternoon. Arriving early helps you get on the popular water rides before the queues grow, especially on hot summer days.

Pack a towel and a change of clothes if your lot plan to tackle the water rides, because getting splashed is very much the point. Sun cream and hats are handy for the outdoor areas, and a light waterproof covers you if the weather turns. With younger children, a pushchair makes the walk between zones easier.
Plan the falconry display into your day as a bit of a breather. Watching birds of prey swoop low over the crowd is a calm, impressive change of pace between the busier rides and play areas.

Dartmouth itself is a real gem. The town tumbles down the hillside to the river, with the grand Britannia Royal Naval College overlooking the water. Wander along the cobbles at Bayard's Cove, follow the river path out to Dartmouth Castle at the mouth of the estuary, or hop on the little ferry across to Kingswear. From Kingswear, the Dartmouth Steam Railway runs along the coast towards Paignton, a lovely treat for train-mad kids.

For beach time, Blackpool Sands near Stoke Fleming is a sheltered cove with clear water, just along the coast. Totnes, upriver, is a quirky market town with a Norman castle and a buzzing high street, perfect for another day.
